# Releasing Vertekum tokens

This workflow applies when the project configures the release extension — `npx vertekum
describe --json` shows it. Without it, stop: this repo has no token release process to run.

## Preconditions

A release describes a **finished** state: `npx vertekum check --json` must pass with zero
errors, and build output must be current and committed, before any release step.

## Severity is derived from the diff, not chosen

The release engine classifies every change against the last released baseline:

| change | severity |
| --- | --- |
| token removed, renamed, or retyped | `major` |
| token added | `minor` |
| value changed | `patch` |

The release severity is the **highest** classification in the diff. Use this vocabulary when
describing the impact of a token change — "this pass renames two tokens, so the token release
is major" — and let the engine compute it rather than asserting it.

## The changelog is part of the release

The engine writes release notes from the classified diff. Do not hand-author changelog entries
for token changes the engine already describes; add prose only for context the diff cannot
carry (why, migrations, deprecation guidance).

## Token severity is not the package bump

The token release and the **package** that ships the tokens are different contracts. The host
repository may version its package by rules that rank the same change differently — a value
change can be a `patch` token release yet a `minor` package bump because it is visible in every
consuming product. **Read the repository’s own contribution docs for its bump policy and
follow them; never assume the two contracts align.** When the repo gives no policy, propose the
token severity as the package bump and say you did so.

## When you are stuck

A release is an outward-facing, hard-to-reverse act. Uncertainty about baseline, severity, or
the package bump is a signal to stop and ask, not to guess.
